finding.claim: StartActionByGet and StartActionByGetAndWait run justification-gated actions with no justification, bypassing the audit requirement enforced on StartAction and StartActionAndWait.
finding.source: Client ActionId in StartActionByGet/StartActionByGetAndWait requests; these RPCs have no justification field.
finding.sink: executor.ExecRequest runs the action; justification is only resolved and logged, never required.

trace.note: FindBindingByID resolves the binding from the client ActionId.
ExecutionRequest built with no Justification.
ExecRequest called without any justification check.
ResolveJustification returns empty string for ordinary users when none is provided.
StartActionByGetAndWait goes through runBindingAndWait (345-358), again with no justification check.

finding.guards_checked: Exec ACL enforced at executor.go:832 (so this bypasses justification, not ACL). StartAction (api.go:161) and StartActionAndWait (api.go:309) call validateJustificationRequired. Restart enforces justification at api_log_arguments.go:50. The ByGet pair omits the check.

finding.claim: Client-supplied HTTP headers set identity: an attacker can impersonate any configured user (including admin-ACL holders) and set Provider to 'system' to bypass the justification check when authHttpHeaderUsername is configured and the listener is reachable without a header-stripping proxy.
finding.source: Request headers named by authHttpHeaderUsername, authHttpHeaderUserGroup, and the literal header 'provider'.
finding.sink: Authenticated identity used for ACL evaluation (acl.go) and justification bypass (IsSystemExecution).

trace.note: Header-based check is first in authChain.
Username taken from configured header.
Provider taken from 'provider' header with no config gate.
User accepted when Username is non-empty.
ACLs built from spoofed username and usergroup.
IsSystemExecution true when Provider == 'system'.
Justification requirement skipped for system executions.

finding.guards_checked: Header auth only active when authHttpHeaderUsername is set (trusted-headers.go:13). No trusted-proxy, IP, or header-origin check anywhere in the path. The provider header has no config gate.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated PasswordHash RPC lets any client occupy the shared 10-slot Argon2 semaphore, causing ResourceExhausted for all LocalUserLogin attempts and sustained CPU/memory load (64 MiB per hash).
finding.source: Any unauthenticated POST to the PasswordHash RPC via /api/.
finding.sink: argon2id.CreateHash under argon2Sem, shared with comparePasswordAndHash used by LocalUserLogin.

trace.note: /api/ routed to connect handler with no auth wrapper.
PasswordHash calls createHash with no UserFromApiCall or ACL check.
CreateHash acquires a slot from argon2Sem (cap 10).
Login path returns ErrArgon2Busy when slots are full.
LocalUserLogin maps ErrArgon2Busy to CodeResourceExhausted.

finding.guards_checked: Concurrency cap of 10 bounds memory (~640 MiB) but there is no authentication, per-client rate limit, or request size limit beyond connect defaults. No auth interceptor found in the mux.

finding.claim: OAuth state, which is the live session credential, and the OAuth authorization code are written to logs, and local session IDs are logged at Warn; log readers can replay the cookie to hijack a victim session.
finding.source: Log readers (anyone with access to log output or the log shipping destination).
finding.sink: logrus output at Infof/Errorf/Debug/Warn containing session credentials.

trace.note: Session cookie olivetin-sid-oauth is set to state.
state logged at Infof on every login start.
Cookie value used directly as session key via lookupOAuth2UserByState (409-424, SID: state).
Query state and cookie value logged at Errorf on mismatch.
OAuth authorization code logged at Debug.
Session sid logged at Warn for stale sessions.
Local session sid logged at Warn.

finding.guards_checked: State comparison at 190-226 is correct. frontend.go:61-80 redacts Authorization and Cookie headers in debug logs, showing intent, but these session-credential log sites are not redacted. Default log level not verified, so Infof exposure is confirmed only at Info level.

finding.claim: anchorCustomRegexPattern skips anchoring when a pattern starts with ^ and ends with $, so top-level alternation such as ^a|b$ is unanchored and passes validation for arbitrary values.
finding.source: Client value for an argument of type regex:<pattern> (admin-authored pattern).
finding.sink: Exec argv element (shell execution blocked for regex types).

trace.note: anchorCustomRegexPattern returns pattern unchanged when it starts with ^ and ends with $.
typeSafetyCheckRegex uses the pattern for custom regex types.
regexp.MatchString with unanchored alternation accepts non-matching values.
checkShellArgumentSafety blocks regex types from shell execution.

finding.guards_checked: Shell execution blocked for regex types (arguments.go:381-403). Argv has no shell interpretation. Impact requires an admin pattern with top-level alternation.

finding.claim: Permissive argument types allow leading '-' or '=' and '/' characters, or skip validation entirely (confirmation/html), so user values can inject options into exec argv where the admin command treats them positionally without a -- terminator.
finding.source: Client argument values for types ascii_sentence, unicode_identifier, email, confirmation, html.

trace.note: unicode_identifier and ascii_sentence regexes permit leading '-'.
confirmation and html skip validation entirely.
email accepted via mail.ParseAddress permitting '-', '=', '/' in local part.
Values placed in argv with no -- terminator.

finding.guards_checked: No shell involved (argv array). Choice-typed arguments enforced exactly (arguments.go:270-282). Impact depends on the admin's command accepting options in that position.

finding.claim: Webhook with empty or 'none' authType accepts all requests, letting anyone trigger the admin-defined action with payload-derived arguments.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /webhooks with a payload matching an ExecOnWebhook config.
finding.sink: Action execution via executeAction with system user 'webhook'.

trace.note: Empty or none authType returns a verifier that always returns true.
processWebhook proceeds on verifier success.
Arguments extracted from payload.
Arguments filtered to declared names via filterToDefinedArguments (175-187).
Shell execution banned for webhook-tagged requests.

finding.guards_checked: Argument typing in executor. Shell banned for webhooks. Payload filtered to declared arguments. ACL for system webhook user still applies. Precondition: webhook configured without authType (GitHub path defaults to HMAC at github.go:33-34).

finding.claim: Local password login has no throttling or lockout, and response timing reveals whether a username exists (Argon2 runs only for existing users), enabling unlimited online guessing and user enumeration.
finding.source: Unauthenticated LocalUserLogin requests with arbitrary username and password.

trace.note: LocalUserLogin entry point with no rate limit.
checkUserPassword returns immediately for unknown users without hashing.
Existing users run Argon2 comparison (timing difference).
Users with no password fast-fail (separate timing oracle).

finding.guards_checked: Argon2 concurrency cap of 10 bounds throughput but is not a per-user or per-client throttle. No lockout or rate limiting found.
